loc: Lesson02_Kubernetes_Foundations_for_Backup_Admins.html · Section 06 · caption under the VolumeSnapshotClass code block
orig: K10 appears inside the annotation key because that is the product's technical namespace in the API; the product name is Veeam Kasten.
prop: k10 appears in lowercase inside the annotation key k10.kasten.io/is-snapshot-class because that key is a verbatim technical string; the product name is Veeam Kasten for Kubernetes.
why: Two problems in one sentence. (1) Naming standard and glossary.md "K10" note: "K10" is permitted only inside verbatim technical strings — but the string in the code block directly above is lowercase (k10.kasten.io/is-snapshot-class), so the caption's uppercase "K10" is not the verbatim string it claims to be and reintroduces the retired product name as prose. (2) "the product's technical namespace in the API" is imprecise — k10.kasten.io is the annotation key's domain prefix, not a Kubernetes namespace, and the module has just spent a section teaching the learner what a namespace is. Same paragraph also carries the only remaining uppercase K10 in the six files, so fixing it clears the naming check course-wide.

loc: Lesson04_Maintaining_Veeam_Kasten_Over_Time.html · Section 03 "Layer one: the dashboard" → Compliant card

prop: A policy applies and its service-level objectives are being respected [Src: Kasten Docs 9.0.2 p.301].

SLA and SLO are not interchangeable terms to a technical audience, and this is the state a learner reads every morning. Standardising on "service-level objectives" (the form in the fullest treatment, Module 05) also aligns with the surrounding RPO/RTO vocabulary. Also apply to Lesson02 l.386: "compliant when a policy applies and its service levels are being met" → "compliant when a policy applies and its service-level objectives are being respected". LXD: confirm the exact wording on p.301 and use that single form in all three places.

loc: Lesson04_Maintaining_Veeam_Kasten_Over_Time.html · Section 03 "Layer one: the dashboard" → Removed card
orig: Objects that have been removed [Src: Kasten Docs 9.0.2 p.301].
prop: Objects that no longer exist on the cluster; filter to this state to find a removed application and restore it [Src: Kasten Docs 9.0.2 p.301, p.397].
why: Circular definition — "Removed means objects that have been removed" teaches nothing, and it sits in a four-card set where the other three states are properly explained. This audience has no Kubernetes background, so the question the card leaves unanswered is the one that matters: does a removed application still have restore points? It does, and Module 05 says so (l.360: removed applications are hidden by default, you filter and select Removed to find them, then use the normal restore workflow, p.397). Pointing forward to that closes the loop rather than repeating the label. The same circularity appears in Lesson05 l.219 ("and Removed, meaning objects that are removed") — fix both to the same wording. Rubric 3 (clarity) and Rubric 2 (comprehension floor).

Worse, at course level Q4 is a near-duplicate of Lesson03's knowledge-check Q5 — same stem premise (selecting a Veeam Repository as the Export Location Profile), same correct answer (block mode export is enabled automatically), same source pages. Retargeting this one item onto the editions closes the objective gap and removes the duplicate in a single change; Q5 already covers the Veeam Backup & Replication integration for objective 5, and the block-mode rule stays taught in Section 05's constraints table.
